newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo platinum group metals fall, gold firmer.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo platinum group metals fall, gold firmer.

text.p: Yen-based Tokyo platinum group metals futures ended lower on Monday, although the yen's fall against the dollar late in the day helped prices rebound from early lows, traders said.
Gold futures ended firmer, buoyed by firmer bullion prices, they said.
Platinum futures ranged from 19 yen to 33 yen per gram lower, with benchmark February ending down 19 yen at 1,490 yen.
"A feeling that prices of platinum group metals were too high after recent sharp gains, prompted individual investors to sell futures aggressively from the opening," one trader said.
Palladium futures ranged from 13 yen to 19 yen per gram lower. Most-active benchmark February was down 18 yen at 572 yen.

Traders said the day's falls of platinum group metals were considered a technical correction after recent robust gains in overheated trade, and lingering uncertainty over Russian metal supply continued to fuel speculative interest.
"Volatile trading in platinum group metals is likely to continue. The downside potential in a technical correction could be limited unless Russia resumes metal exports to Japan," another trader said.
The market was watching for further developments at Russian producer Norilsk, where workers adopted a strike plan over the weekend, the traders said.
In contrast to animated trading of platinum group metals, trading in gold futures was lacklustre and featureless.
In the bullion market, spot gold was quoted at $362.40/70 per ounce at the Tokyo close, against $363.00/363.50 in New York on Friday.
Benchmark February silver futures ended up 0.8 yen per 10 grams at 206.5 yen.
